elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "shall be exercisable in respect of any Party no more than once in any calendar year" — a calendar-year cap satisfies the once-per-12-month frequency limit in substance.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted language gives "not less than fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" — 15 days, short of the preferred 30 days.
Neither 9.8, 9.9 nor the inserted sentence contains any business-hours limitation; the drafter expressly declined to press it.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 9.9 channels audits through the F&ASC (a committee of the Parties), not an independent auditor, and no independence requirement was added.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality undertaking for the reviewing Party or the F&ASC appears in the cited or inserted text.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site preference language anywhere in Paragraph 9 or the insertion.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 9.8: the audited Party "shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit", with no underpayment shift-back — the requesting (auditing) Party bears cost unconditionally, which satisfies and exceeds the 5% formulation.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The audit right in 9.8 is confined to "the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs"; no access to systems or remote access is granted, and nothing was added that would grant it.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "exercisable in respect of any Party no more than once in any calendar year".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "only upon not less than fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to that Party" — meets and (by being written) exceeds the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Existing 9.8 makes the requesting Party bear the audited Party's entire reasonable compliance costs with no underpayment carve-out; more favourable than the fallback and correctly left untouched.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the face of the operative language: the single inserted sentence supplies the once-per-calendar-year frequency cap and the 15 days' prior written notice, and retained 9.8 already allocates the entire reasonable compliance cost to the requesting Party with no underpayment shift-back, which satisfies (and exceeds) the 10% cost element.

Preferred level is not complete: notice remains 15 days rather than 30; there is no business-hours window, no independent-auditor requirement (9.9 routes audits through the F&ASC, a Party committee), no auditor confidentiality undertaking, and no off-site preference. To reach preferred the drafter would have to amend the inserted sentence to thirty (30) days and add operative words requiring audits during Customer's normal business hours, by an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, conducted off-site where reasonably possible.

Minimality holds: nothing was deleted, 9.8 and 9.9 survive verbatim, and the insertion adds only the two missing fallback mechanics. No survival tail, expense allocation, remedy or procedure was bolted on. The symmetric drafting ("in respect of any Party") is the natural implementation of the limit in a reciprocal multi-Party audit regime rather than an extra requirement, though the drafter should be aware it also caps our own audit right against the other Parties.

Intent is preserved: cost allocation in 9.8, the F&ASC-channelling requirement in 9.9, the Schedule B proportions and the separate Paragraph 10.8 maintenance-records inspection right all survive without contradiction, and the insertion creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.

Drafting nit to fix before sending: the margin comment describes the insertion as a new 9.10, but the rendered text appends it as an unnumbered paragraph after 9.9. Number it 9.10 so the cap is separately citable and cannot be read as a continuation of 9.9's F&ASC-procedure sentence.
